MEASURED -- the destructor is declared INLINE in include/daObjTdFuta_c.h on purpose. With the body out of line mwccarm 2004/b56 emits D0 ahead of D1 and the cartridge has D1 first, which rombuild refuses outright; an inline body emits D1 then D0 and no D2, exactly the set and the order ov032 carries. The cost is that `tubuild linkcheck --partial` is impossible for this TU, so its evidence is a full `linkcheck --baseline --module ov032` run after promotion plus rombuild 106/106.
The class adds no storage: the factory's own allocation literal is 0x320, which is dBgActor_c's size, and the size assert in the header closes on it.

The two SharedFilePtr globals data_ov032_02113acc / data_ov032_02113ad4 were spelled `extern "C"` by the destructor and cleanup sources and plain `extern` by InitResources; both name the same unmangled ov032 data symbol, so the C-linkage spelling is the true one and tubuild's reported conflict was cosmetic.

FOLD 2026-09-04. daObjTdFuta_c_classInit at 0x02112668 (historical alias HugeCover_Spawn) was folded in from src/daObjTdFuta_c_classInit.c. It is the TD_FUTA registry profile's factory and sits immediately after InitResources in the ROM's .text order, so it was always part of this TU; it was left outside only because the promotion predated the profile-reconstruction campaign. Folding it is what frees the d_a_obj_td_futa stem, which tools/layout_check.py L2 would otherwise refuse to let the one-function source take. It keeps C linkage and its own extern declarations are restated in this TU rather than pulled in through a decl_*.h.
